text:
Frederick Gaudreau was never drafted. He worked his way up through Milwaukee in the AHL, and at 33 he has 8 goals in 21 games for Seattle, already more than the 7 he scored in 68 games last season. He is doing it on a line that rarely has the puck: with him on at five on five, the Kraken have only 35.7% of the shot attempts.

Our numbers say the finishing is the part to doubt. He's shooting 38% on 21 shots, against 10% last season, from 4.19 expected goals (the quality of his chances). The chances are better than usual for him, but that rate rarely lasts. There's luck pulling the other way too: Seattle has scored 5.4 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which tends to even out. Evolving-Hockey had him playing with weak teammates last season (bottom 5%), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking marks him as a passer from behind the net, 20% of his setups against 8% for a typical forward. Alison Lukan saw that side on Nov. 19, noting his "classy final setup" on Berkly Catton's hat trick in a 5-1 win.
headline: Frederick Gaudreau's hot finish meets cold numbers
